data.title: Diff
data.tagline: See exactly what changed between two states
data.description: A diff shows added, removed, and modified lines between the working tree, staged changes, commits, or branches. Read it before committing and reviewing so accidental edits, secrets, and unrelated changes are caught early.

use: Find an accidental or missing change
avoid: Review only the filenames and skip the actual lines
Assume a small diff has a small product impact
Include formatting changes that hide the real edit
Copy secrets into a diff shared outside the team

lessonPractice.title: An Agent says it only changed a button color, but `git status` shows 12 changed files and large deletions. What should happen before commit?

options.label: Review unstaged and staged diffs line by line for deletion, debug content, and secrets
options.feedback: Diff shows actual additions and removals, and both areas reveal what the final commit will contain.

options.label: Check only the file count and commit as long as the button file appears
options.feedback: Filenames do not reveal line changes, so other files may still contain deletion or sensitive content.

options.label: Assume many green additions mean correctness and skip reading removed content
options.feedback: Colors indicate addition and removal, not business correctness; large deletions require explicit review.

data.agentPrompt: Before commit, show unstaged and staged diffs separately, explain each file, and flag anything beyond button color. Check large deletions, debug text, generated files, and real secrets, and wait for scope confirmation.
